1	# Agent usage — `internal/agentusage`
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	Two pieces: the data layer `internal/agentusage` (sections up to
7	"Verification") and the `:agent-usage` view `internal/ui/agentusageview`
8	(last section, DEVDESK-41).
9	
10	## What the package is for
11	
12	`internal/agentusage` reads the transcripts Claude Code writes under its
13	projects directory and returns, for one session, the **token counts per
14	agent** (the orchestrator and each sub-agent). It is the data layer of the
15	agent usage monitor (DEVDESK-40, spike S-01 then step S-02).
16	
17	What it does **not** do:
18	
19	- no cost, price or quota computation;
20	- no storage, no cache, nothing written to disk;
21	- no UI, no Bubble Tea import (the view lives in `internal/ui/agentusageview`);
22	- no dependency beyond the Go standard library.
23	
24	**The public API is a contract.** Every exported symbol in the table below
25	(`Tokens`, `Agent`, `State`, `Usage`, `Diagnostics`, `FileIssue`, `IssueKind`,
26	`SessionFiles`, `SubAgentFiles`, `ParseSession`, `LocateSession`, `ProjectsRoot`,
27	`ListSessions`, `Session`, `Listing`)
28	is consumed by S-03b, S-04 and S-05a. Changing a field is a change to those
29	stories; add, do not rename.
30	
31	## Public API
32	
33	| Symbol | Role |
34	|---|---|
35	| `ProjectsRoot()` | `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, else `~/.claude/projects` |
36	| `LocateSession(parentTranscript)` | from `<dir>/<uuid>.jsonl`, finds `<dir>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and their meta files. Returns `SessionFiles{ID, Parent, SubAgents}`. A missing session directory means no sub-agents. Returns an error if the parent is missing, is a symbolic link or is not a regular file. |
37	| `SessionFiles` | `ID`, `Parent` (path of the parent transcript), `SubAgents []SubAgentFiles` |
38	| `SubAgentFiles` | `ID`, `Transcript`, `Meta` (`""` if the meta file is absent) |
39	| `ParseSession(SessionFiles)` | returns `Usage`. Fails only if the parent transcript cannot be opened: a missing file, a symbolic link or a non-regular file is an **error**, not an ignored input. |
40	| `ListSessions(root)` | lists `<root>/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl`, one level deep, never recursively. Returns `Listing`. A missing root is an empty `Listing` and no error; a root that is not a directory or cannot be read is an error naming the base name only. The root itself may be a symbolic link (the user's own choice); anything below it may not. |
41	| `Session{ID, Parent, Project, ModTime}` | `Parent` is a full path, for `LocateSession`, and is never logged. `Project` is the working directory read from the transcript (`cwd`), sanitized and capped at 4096 bytes, or `""` if none. `ModTime` is the transcript's modification time. |
42	| `Listing{Sessions, Omitted}` | `Sessions` newest `ModTime` first, ties by ID ascending. `Omitted` counts what was not listed: linked or non-regular transcripts, linked or unreadable project directories, and sessions past the cap. |
43	| `Tokens{Input, Output, CacheRead, CacheWrite}` | `int64` counters; `Total()` and `Add()` saturate at `math.MaxInt64` |
44	| `Agent` | `ID` (empty for the orchestrator), `Main`, `Type`, `Models`, `Tokens`, `Messages`, `PartialMessages`, `State`, `SpawnDepth`; `PartialOutput()` |
45	| `State` | `StateUnknown`, `StateFinished`, `StateUnfinished` |
46	| `Usage` | `SessionID`, `Agents` (orchestrator first, then sub-agents by ID), `Versions`, `Diagnostics`; `Total()` |
47	| `Diagnostics` | `UnreadableLines`, `OversizedLines`, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, `MetaMissing`, `MetaUnreadable`, `TruncatedFiles`, `Files []FileIssue`; `Degraded()` |
48	| `FileIssue{File, Offset, Kind}` | one skipped line or file problem. `File` is a base name. `Offset` is the byte offset of the line (for `IssueReadError`, the offset consumed; for `IssueOpenFailed`, 0). Entries are sorted by offset within each file. |
49	| `IssueKind` | `IssueUnreadable` (not JSON, truncated, or bad counters), `IssueOversized` (longer than `MaxLineBytes`), `IssueOpenFailed` (a sub-agent transcript could not be opened), `IssueReadError` (reading stopped on an I/O error) |
50	
51	`State` is read from the `finished` key of the sub-agent's meta file: `true`
52	is `StateFinished`, `false` is `StateUnfinished`. An absent, null or
53	wrongly typed key, a missing or unreadable meta file, and the orchestrator
54	are `StateUnknown`.
55	
56	## Transcript format
57	
58	```
59	projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl                          orchestrator
60	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl     one per sub-agent
61	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json agentType, finished, spawnDepth
62	projects/<project>/<uuid>/tool-results/                  never read
63	```
64	
65	Each transcript line is a JSON object. Only `version` and `message.{id, model,
66	stop_reason, usage}` are read; the four counters are `input_tokens`,
67	`output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
68	Content, tools and descriptions are not declared in the decoding structs, so
69	`encoding/json` skips them without keeping them. Nothing is searched
70	recursively. Symbolic links are handled by position:
71	
72	- a **parent transcript** that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is an
73	  **error** (`LocateSession` and `ParseSession`);
74	- a sub-agent transcript that is a link or not a regular file is not listed by
75	  `LocateSession`; if one is passed to `ParseSession` anyway, it stays in
76	  `Agents` with an `IssueOpenFailed` entry;
77	- a meta file that is a link or not a regular file counts as missing
78	  (`MetaMissing`);
79	- a session directory or `subagents/` directory that is a link means no
80	  sub-agents.
81	
82	## Aggregation rules
83	
84	- **Last line wins per `message.id`**, over the whole session. Streaming writes
85	  the same message several times; only the final state counts.
86	- **A message seen in several files is attributed to the last file read**
87	  (orchestrator first, then sub-agents sorted by ID). Each such overwrite counts
88	  in `Diagnostics.CrossFileDuplicates`.
89	- **A line without `message.id` counts once**, keyed by file and offset, and
90	  increments `NoMessageID`.
91	- **`<synthetic>` is excluded**: locally generated turns are never billed.
92	- **A line with neither id, model nor usage is ignored** (user and tool-result
93	  lines).
94	- **Partial output**: a message whose last line has a null or absent
95	  `stop_reason` is counted in `Agent.PartialMessages`, and `PartialOutput()` is
96	  true. Its output count is a floor. This is computed for every agent; the UI
97	  decides how to show it.
98	- **Saturation**: sums stop at `math.MaxInt64` instead of wrapping.
99	- An incomplete last line (no newline) is not counted and its file is listed in
100	  `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles`. If it already exceeds the line cap it is dropped
101	  silently.
102	
103	## Tolerance
104	
105	The format is not a documented API, so the parser degrades rather than fails.
106	
107	- Unknown fields are ignored.
108	- A message with an id or model but **no `usage`** (absent, or renamed by a
109	  newer client) is counted in `Diagnostics.NoUsage` and adds nothing. A
110	  sub-agent with no usable meta `finished` is `StateUnknown`.
111	- Metadata of an unexpected type (`model`, `version`, `agentType`,
112	  `spawnDepth`) costs that field only, not the line.
113	- A counter that is negative, fractional or not a number makes the line
114	  unreadable (`UnreadableLines`). An absent or null counter is 0.
115	- A sub-agent that cannot be opened stays in `Agents` with no tokens and an
116	  `IssueOpenFailed` entry. A read error mid-file keeps what was read and adds
117	  `IssueReadError` at the offset consumed.
118	- A missing meta file counts in `MetaMissing`; an unreadable one in
119	  `MetaUnreadable`.
120	
121	## Privacy
122	
123	`ParseSession` returns **numeric aggregates only**. No prompt, answer, tool
124	input, description or path is ever stored in a `Usage`.
125	
126	**Amendment (DEVDESK-41): `cwd` is now read and displayed.** `ListSessions`
127	alone reads it, to tell sessions apart by project. It is the first non-empty
128	string `cwd` found in the first 8 MiB of a transcript (twice `MaxLineBytes`, so
129	one maximal line can be skipped); the scan stops there and nothing else of the
130	transcript is kept. The view shows the **full path**, with the home folder
131	folded to `~`. The path is sanitized and capped, and is **never logged**: the
132	view logs a failed listing, but its error carries a base name only. A `Usage`
133	still carries no path. This replaces the earlier wording that no path was ever
134	read.
135	
136	- Errors carry the base name of a file, never its full path (`baseOnly`), and
137	  fixed messages instead of `encoding/json` errors, which can quote content.
138	- Text that comes from disk goes through `sanitize`: labels (model, version,
139	  agent type, session and agent IDs, file names; `sanitizeLabel`, cut to 128
140	  bytes) and the `cwd` (cut to 4096 bytes). Replaced by `?`: invalid UTF-8
141	  bytes, every control character (C0, DEL and **C1**, so a raw or encoded
142	  0x9B CSI is caught) and every format character (Unicode category **Cf**:
143	  bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width marks). Text read from disk reaches a
144	  terminal, where an escape sequence would be interpreted and a bidi override
145	  would reorder what follows.
146	- `FileIssue.File` is a base name, never a path.
147	- The fixtures plant `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` in the `content`, `description`,
148	  `cwd` and tool `input` fields of the transcripts and in the `description`
149	  of the `.meta.json` files. Tests check that it never appears in a `Usage` or
150	  an error.
151	
152	## Limits and caps
153	
154	Memory and output size do not depend on what a transcript contains.
155	
156	| Bound | Value | Behavior past it |
157	|---|---|---|
158	| Line length (`MaxLineBytes`) | 4 MiB | line skipped, counted in `OversizedLines`, never held in memory |
159	| `FileIssue` entries per file | 100, for `IssueUnreadable` and `IssueOversized` only | counters keep counting, entries stop. `IssueOpenFailed` and `IssueReadError` occur once per file and are always kept |
160	| Lines without id in the table | 100000, for the whole session (all files together) | still counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`, but aggregated without a table entry |
161	| Models per agent / versions per session | 64 | extra ones dropped |
162	| Label length | 128 bytes | truncated |
163	| Meta file | 1 MiB | refused (`MetaUnreadable`) |
164	| Sessions listed (`ListSessions`) | 10000 | the oldest are dropped and counted in `Listing.Omitted` |
165	| `cwd` probe (`ListSessions`) | first 8 MiB of each kept transcript | `Project` is `""` |
166	| `Session.Project` length | 4096 bytes | truncated |
167	
168	The 10000 cap applies after the directories are read: there is **no bound on
169	memory or time before it**. Every entry of every project directory is read and
170	stat-ed first, so a very large projects tree costs that much before the cap
171	trims the result. Only the `cwd` probe, run on the kept sessions, is bounded.
172	
173	## Known risk: a FIFO swapped in between `Lstat` and `Open`
174	
175	`openPlain` (`safeopen.go`) calls `Lstat`, refuses links and non-regular
176	files, opens the file, then compares the handle with the `Lstat` result using
177	`os.SameFile`. That closes the check-then-open window for links. It does not
178	for a regular file replaced by a **FIFO** between `Lstat` and `Open`: `os.Open`
179	blocks until a writer appears, before `SameFile` can run. Closing it would need
180	`O_NONBLOCK`, which the `os` package does not offer portably. The window is tiny
181	and the attacker must already control the transcripts directory. Accepted and
182	documented in the code. `ListSessions` has the same exposure: it opens each
183	kept transcript through `openPlain` to read its `cwd`, so a FIFO swapped in
184	there can block the listing (and so the view's read, which runs in a `Cmd`).
185	Carried over unchanged, not closed.
186	
187	## Diagnostics and `Degraded`
188	
189	`Diagnostics.Degraded()` is true if anything was skipped or guessed: unreadable
190	or oversized lines, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, meta
191	missing or unreadable, truncated files, or any `FileIssue`. A consumer should
192	show the totals as usual and flag them as approximate when it is true. A new
193	counter must be added to `Degraded()`.
194	
195	## Verification
196	
197	- **Spike S-01**: the parsing rules were checked against ccusage on 3 real
198	  sessions, with a **0.00 %** difference.
199	- **Fixtures** in `internal/agentusage/testdata/` are synthetic: shape follows
200	  Claude Code 2.1.302, every value is invented. `v2.1.302-basic/`,
201	  `synthetic-other-version/` (renamed or absent usage, unknown line type) and
202	  `damaged/` (bad line, file cut mid-JSON). Expected totals are written by hand
203	  in `parse_test.go`. See `testdata/README.md`.
204	- **Cross-check against ccusage** (step 6 of S-02, DEVDESK-54), reference
205	  version `ccusage@20.0.43`. `crosscheck_test.go` compares `ParseSession` with
206	  a reference file and is **skipped unless `DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF` is set**
207	  (path of the reference file). CI never sets it, so **CI does not run this
208	  test**: run it by hand. `DEVDESK_CLAUDE_PROJECTS` points to the projects
209	  directory to read (default: `ProjectsRoot()`). Each session is looked up as
210	  `<root>/<project>/<id>.jsonl`.
211	  The reference file is produced by the `mise` task:
212	
213	  ```bash
214	  mise run agentusage-ref -- <uuid>... > /path/outside/repo/ref.json
215	  DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF=/path/outside/repo/ref.json go test ./internal/agentusage -run TestSessionTotalsMatchCcusage -v
216	  ```
217	
218	  The task needs a POSIX shell, `npx` and `jq` (no Windows), and runs with
219	  `set -euo pipefail`: a failing ccusage call fails the task. For each session
220	  id it runs `ccusage claude session --id <uuid> --json` and writes
221	  `{"sessions": [{id, total, input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, ...]}`,
222	  where `total` is ccusage's `totalTokens` and the four others are sums over its
223	  `entries`. Write the file **outside the repository**: it comes from real
224	  sessions and must never be committed.
225	
226	  Only `total` is required. `input`, `output`, `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite` are
227	  optional per session: when present, each is compared too, and each must be
228	  within the tolerance (2 %, strictly below). A session whose transcript is not
229	  found, or whose parsing fails, fails the test.
230	
231	## The `:agent-usage` view
232	
233	`internal/ui/agentusageview`, opened with `:agent-usage` or `:au`. It lists the
234	Claude Code sessions found on this machine, newest first, and reads only where
235	and when a session ran (see the privacy amendment above). No token count is
236	shown yet.
237	
238	| Column | Content |
239	|---|---|
240	| Project | the `cwd`, **full path** with home folded to `~` (`theme.FoldHome`, done once per row in `Update`, never in a `Cell`). Cut from the left when too narrow, so the leaf stays visible. `-` (dim) when the transcript named none. |
241	| Last active | the transcript's `ModTime`, local time, `2006-01-02 15:04` |
242	| Session | the first 8 characters of the ID. `Optional`: the first column dropped on a narrow terminal. The filter (`/`) matches the full ID. |
243	
244	- **Rule 139.** The body is always `m.table.View()`. Loading, an empty
245	  machine and a filter with no match all leave a table with its header.
246	- **Header** (`GetHeaderInfo`): `Sessions` (rows visible after the filter) and,
247	  only when non-zero, `Skipped` (`Listing.Omitted`).
248	- **Footer** (Rule 128), derived on every frame with no timer, in this order:
249	  a failed read (red, "Failed to list Claude Code sessions — check logs"; the
250	  error is logged, never shown, since it can name a path), then loading (spinner,
251	  "Reading Claude Code sessions..."), then "No Claude Code sessions found in
252	  <root>" when the listing is empty before any filter.
253	- **Shortcuts**: `ctrl+r` Refresh, `/` Filter, `?` Help. The same keys in every
254	  state, none greyed (Rule 130): each always acts. `.` cycles the sort column
255	  and is listed in `?` only (Rule 138).
256	- **Reload on every entry.** The view is built once and stays cached in the
257	  router (`createView` stops if it already exists). The reload comes from
258	  `switchView` (`internal/app/command_line.go`), which calls `Init()` on every
259	  entry, and `Init` starts a read. The rows from the previous visit stay on
260	  screen until the answer arrives. Unlike `ctrl+r`, this entry reload shows no
261	  spinner and no "Reading..." line, because `Init` cannot set `loading` to
262	  true. `ctrl+r` reads again under a new generation number, and a stale answer
263	  (older generation) is dropped. A failed refresh keeps the previous rows: they
264	  are dated, not wrong.
265	- **Rule 110.** `listSessionsCmd` resolves `ProjectsRoot()` and calls
266	  `ListSessions` inside the `Cmd` and returns a message; `Update` alone touches
267	  the model.
268	
269	Known limits: the FIFO risk and the lack of a memory or time bound before the
270	10000-session cap (see "Limits and caps") both apply to this view's read. Claude
271	Code deletes old transcripts itself (30 days by default), so older sessions
272	disappear from the list.
273	package agentusage
274	
275	// Agent is the usage of one agent of a session: the orchestrator (Main) or a
276	// sub-agent.
277	type Agent struct {
278		ID              string
279		Main            bool
280		Type            string // sub-agent type from its meta file; "" if unknown
281		Models          []string
282		Tokens          Tokens
283		Messages        int // distinct message ids
284		PartialMessages int // messages whose last line has no stop reason
285		State           State
286		SpawnDepth      int
287	}
288	
289	// PartialOutput reports whether some message of the agent was still being
290	// written (no stop reason on its last line), so its output count is a floor.
291	func (a Agent) PartialOutput() bool { return a.PartialMessages > 0 }
292	
293	// IssueKind classifies a line that could not be counted.
294	type IssueKind int
295	
296	const (
297		IssueUnreadable IssueKind = iota // not JSON, truncated, or bad counters
298		IssueOversized                   // longer than MaxLineBytes
299		IssueOpenFailed                  // a sub-agent transcript could not be opened
300		IssueReadError                   // reading stopped on an I/O error at Offset
301	)
302	
303	// FileIssue locates one skipped line. File is a base name, never a path.
304	type FileIssue struct {
305		File   string
306		Offset int64
307		Kind   IssueKind
308	}
309	
310	// Diagnostics counts what parsing skipped or had to guess.
311	type Diagnostics struct {
312		UnreadableLines     int
313		OversizedLines      int
314		NoUsage             int
315		NoMessageID         int
316		CrossFileDuplicates int
317		MetaMissing         int
318		MetaUnreadable      int
319		TruncatedFiles      []string
320		Files               []FileIssue
321	}
322	
323	// Degraded reports whether anything was skipped or guessed.
324	func (d Diagnostics) Degraded() bool {
325		return d.UnreadableLines > 0 || d.OversizedLines > 0 || d.NoUsage > 0 ||
326			d.NoMessageID > 0 || d.CrossFileDuplicates > 0 || d.MetaMissing > 0 ||
327			d.MetaUnreadable > 0 || len(d.TruncatedFiles) > 0 || len(d.Files) > 0
328	}
329	
330	// Usage is the parsed usage of one session.
331	type Usage struct {
332		SessionID   string
333		Agents      []Agent
334		Versions    []string
335		Diagnostics Diagnostics
336	}
337	
338	// Total returns the tokens of every agent.
339	func (u Usage) Total() Tokens {
340		var t Tokens
341		for _, a := range u.Agents {
342			t = t.Add(a.Tokens)
343		}
344		return t
345	}
346	package agentusage
347	
348	// msgKey identifies one message of a session. A message with an id is keyed
349	// by the id alone; one without is keyed by where it was read.
350	type msgKey struct {
351		id   string
352		file string
353		off  int64
354	}
355	
356	// entry is the last state seen of one message.
357	type entry struct {
358		agent    int
359		file     string
360		model    string
361		tokens   Tokens
362		stopNull bool
363	}
364	
365	// aggregator folds records into per-agent totals, last line wins per
366	// message id. Agents must be added in a fixed order (parent, then
367	// sub-agents by ID); a message seen in several files goes to the last.
368	type aggregator struct {
369		agents  []Agent
370		diag    Diagnostics
371		entries map[msgKey]*entry
372		order   []msgKey // first appearance, for stable model order
373		seen    map[string]bool
374		version []string // distinct versions, first appearance order
375		// fileIssues counts the capped FileIssue kinds kept per file name.
376		fileIssues map[string]int
377		noID       int            // table entries holding a line without message id
378		spill      map[int]*spill // per agent: no-id lines past maxNoIDEntries
379	}
380	
381	// spill totals the lines that no longer get a table entry.
382	type spill struct {
383		tokens   Tokens
384		messages int
385		partial  int
386		models   modelSet
387	}
388	
389	// newAggregator starts from agents carrying their identity (ID, Main, Type,
390	// State, SpawnDepth); the counters are filled by add and finish.
391	func newAggregator(agents []Agent) *aggregator {
392		return &aggregator{
393			agents: agents, entries: map[msgKey]*entry{}, seen: map[string]bool{},
394			fileIssues: map[string]int{}, spill: map[int]*spill{},
395		}
396	}
397	
398	// addIssue records a skipped line. Unreadable and oversized lines are kept
399	// at most maxFileIssuesPerFile per file (the counters are not capped); the
400	// other kinds occur once per file and are always kept.
401	func (a *aggregator) addIssue(i FileIssue) {
402		if i.Kind == IssueUnreadable || i.Kind == IssueOversized {
403			if a.fileIssues[i.File] >= maxFileIssuesPerFile {
404				return
405			}
406			a.fileIssues[i.File]++
407		}
408		a.diag.Files = append(a.diag.Files, i)
409	}
410	
411	// addLine decodes one line of agent agentIdx's file (file is a base name) and folds it in,
412	// counting what is skipped. Synthetic and ignored lines never count.
413	func (a *aggregator) addLine(agentIdx int, file string, off int64, line []byte) {
414		r, kind := decodeLine(line)
415		if kind != kindUnreadable {
416			a.noteVersion(r.Version)
417		}
418		switch kind {
419		case kindUsage:
420			a.add(agentIdx, file, off, r)
421		case kindNoUsage:
422			a.diag.NoUsage++
423		case kindUnreadable:
424			a.diag.UnreadableLines++
425			a.addIssue(FileIssue{File: file, Offset: off, Kind: IssueUnreadable})
426		case kindIgnored, kindSynthetic:
427		}
428	}
429	
430	// noteVersion records a client version the first time it is seen, up to
431	// maxVersions.
432	func (a *aggregator) noteVersion(v string) {
433		v = sanitizeLabel(v)
434		if v == "" || a.seen[v] || len(a.version) >= maxVersions {
435			return
436		}
437		a.seen[v] = true
438		a.version = append(a.version, v)
439	}
440	
441	// versions returns the distinct versions seen, in order of first appearance.
442	func (a *aggregator) versions() []string { return a.version }
443	
444	// add folds one usage record in. file and off identify the line when the
445	// record has no message id.
446	func (a *aggregator) add(agentIdx int, file string, off int64, r record) {
447		key := msgKey{id: r.MessageID}
448		if r.MessageID == "" {
449			key = msgKey{file: file, off: off}
450			a.diag.NoMessageID++
451			if a.noID >= maxNoIDEntries {
452				a.addSpill(agentIdx, r)
453				return
454			}
455			a.noID++
456		}
457		e, ok := a.entries[key]
458		if !ok {
459			e = &entry{}
460			a.entries[key] = e
461			a.order = append(a.order, key)
462		} else if e.file != file {
463			a.diag.CrossFileDuplicates++
464		}
465		*e = entry{agent: agentIdx, file: file, model: r.Model, tokens: r.Usage, stopNull: r.StopNull}
466	}
467	
468	// addSpill counts a no-id line that gets no table entry.
469	func (a *aggregator) addSpill(agentIdx int, r record) {
470		sp := a.spill[agentIdx]
471		if sp == nil {
472			sp = &spill{}
473			a.spill[agentIdx] = sp
474		}
475		sp.tokens = sp.tokens.Add(r.Usage)
476		sp.messages++
477		if r.StopNull {
478			sp.partial++
479		}
480		sp.models.add(r.Model)
481	}
482	
483	// finish returns the agents with Tokens, Models, Messages and
484	// PartialMessages computed.
485	func (a *aggregator) finish() []Agent {
486		models := make([]modelSet, len(a.agents))
487		for i := range a.agents {
488			a.agents[i].Tokens, a.agents[i].Models = Tokens{}, nil
489			a.agents[i].Messages, a.agents[i].PartialMessages = 0, 0
490		}
491		for _, key := range a.order {
492			e := a.entries[key]
493			ag := &a.agents[e.agent]
494			ag.Tokens = ag.Tokens.Add(e.tokens)
495			ag.Messages++
496			if e.stopNull {
497				ag.PartialMessages++
498			}
499			models[e.agent].add(e.model)
500		}
501		for i, sp := range a.spill {
502			ag := &a.agents[i]
503			ag.Tokens = ag.Tokens.Add(sp.tokens)
504			ag.Messages += sp.messages
505			ag.PartialMessages += sp.partial
506			for _, m := range sp.models.list {
507				models[i].add(m)
508			}
509		}
510		for i := range a.agents {
511			a.agents[i].Models = models[i].list
512		}
513		return a.agents
514	}
515	package agentusage
516	
517	import (
518		"io"
519		"path/filepath"
520		"sort"
521	)
522	
523	// ParseSession aggregates the usage of every agent of a session. It fails
524	// only if the parent transcript cannot be opened; a sub-agent that cannot be
525	// read stays in Agents with no tokens and a FileIssue.
526	func ParseSession(files SessionFiles) (Usage, error) {
527		subs := append([]SubAgentFiles(nil), files.SubAgents...)
528		sort.Slice(subs, func(i, j int) bool { return subs[i].ID < subs[j].ID })
529		agg := newAggregator([]Agent{{Main: true, State: StateUnknown}})
530		if err := parseFile(agg, 0, files.Parent); err != nil {
531			return Usage{}, baseOnly(err)
532		}
533		for _, sa := range subs {
534			agg.agents = append(agg.agents, agentFromMeta(&agg.diag, sa))
535			if err := parseFile(agg, len(agg.agents)-1, sa.Transcript); err != nil {
536				agg.addIssue(FileIssue{File: sanitizeLabel(filepath.Base(sa.Transcript)), Kind: IssueOpenFailed})
537			}
538		}
539		return Usage{
540			SessionID:   sanitizeLabel(files.ID),
541			Agents:      agg.finish(),
542			Versions:    agg.versions(),
543			Diagnostics: agg.diag,
544		}, nil
545	}
546	
547	// agentFromMeta builds a sub-agent's identity from its meta file, counting
548	// a missing or unreadable one in diag.
549	func agentFromMeta(diag *Diagnostics, sa SubAgentFiles) Agent {
550		ag := Agent{ID: sanitizeLabel(sa.ID)}
551		if sa.Meta == "" {
552			diag.MetaMissing++
553			return ag
554		}
555		m, err := readMeta(sa.Meta)
556		if err != nil {
557			diag.MetaUnreadable++
558			return ag
559		}
560		ag.Type, ag.State, ag.SpawnDepth = m.AgentType, m.state(), m.SpawnDepth
561		return ag
562	}
563	
564	// parseFile folds one transcript into the aggregator for agent idx. It
565	// fails only if the file cannot be opened.
566	func parseFile(agg *aggregator, idx int, path string) error {
567		f, err := openPlain(path, false)
568		if err != nil {
569			return err
570		}
571		if f == nil {
572			return errNotRegular
573		}
574		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
575		parseReader(agg, idx, sanitizeLabel(filepath.Base(path)), f)
576		return nil
577	}
578	
579	// parseReader folds r into agg for agent idx; name is the file's sanitized
580	// base name. A read error mid-stream keeps what was read and is recorded as
581	// an IssueReadError at the offset consumed; it is not an unreadable line.
582	func parseReader(agg *aggregator, idx int, name string, r io.Reader) {
583		start := len(agg.diag.Files)
584		res, err := scanLines(r, MaxLineBytes, func(line []byte, off int64) {
585			agg.addLine(idx, name, off, line)
586		})
587		for _, off := range res.OversizedAt {
588			agg.diag.OversizedLines++
589			agg.addIssue(FileIssue{File: name, Offset: off, Kind: IssueOversized})
590		}
591		if err != nil {
592			agg.addIssue(FileIssue{File: name, Offset: res.Consumed, Kind: IssueReadError})
593		}
594		if len(res.Tail) > 0 {
595			agg.diag.TruncatedFiles = append(agg.diag.TruncatedFiles, name)
596		}
597		issues := agg.diag.Files[start:]
598		sort.SliceStable(issues, func(i, j int) bool { return issues[i].Offset < issues[j].Offset })
599	}
600	package agentusage
601	
602	import (
603		"errors"
604		"fmt"
605		"io/fs"
606		"os"
607		"path/filepath"
608		"sort"
609		"strings"
610	)
611	
612	const (
613		transcriptExt = ".jsonl"
614		metaExt       = ".meta.json"
615		agentPrefix   = "agent-"
616		subagentsDir  = "subagents"
617	)
618	
619	// SubAgentFiles locates one sub-agent's files; Meta is "" if absent.
620	type SubAgentFiles struct{ ID, Transcript, Meta string }
621	
622	// SessionFiles locates a session's transcripts.
623	type SessionFiles struct {
624		ID, Parent string
625		SubAgents  []SubAgentFiles
626	}
627	
628	// ProjectsRoot returns the Claude Code projects directory:
629	// $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects, else ~/.claude/projects.
630	func ProjectsRoot() (string, error) {
631		if dir := os.Getenv("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"); dir != "" {
632			return filepath.Join(dir, "projects"), nil
633		}
634		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
635		if err != nil {
636			return "", err
637		}
638		return filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "projects"), nil
639	}
640	
641	// LocateSession finds the sub-agent files of the session whose parent
642	// transcript is <dir>/<uuid>.jsonl, looking in <dir>/<uuid>/subagents/. A
643	// missing session directory means no sub-agents. Symbolic links are ignored
644	// and nothing is searched recursively.
645	func LocateSession(parentTranscript string) (SessionFiles, error) {
646		base := filepath.Base(parentTranscript)
647		if !strings.HasSuffix(base, transcriptExt) {
648			return SessionFiles{}, fmt.Errorf("agentusage: %s does not end in %s", base, transcriptExt)
649		}
650		info, err := os.Lstat(parentTranscript)
651		if err != nil {
652			return SessionFiles{}, baseOnly(err)
653		}
654		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
655			return SessionFiles{}, fmt.Errorf("agentusage: %s is not a regular file", base)
656		}
657		id := strings.TrimSuffix(base, transcriptExt)
658		if id == "" {
659			return SessionFiles{}, fmt.Errorf("agentusage: %s has no session id", base)
660		}
661		files := SessionFiles{ID: sanitizeLabel(id), Parent: parentTranscript}
662		sessionDir := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(parentTranscript), id)
663		if fi, err := os.Lstat(sessionDir); err != nil || !fi.IsDir() {
664			if err == nil || errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
665				return files, nil // absent, or a link: no sub-agents
666			}
667			return files, baseOnly(err)
668		}
669		files.SubAgents, err = subAgentFiles(filepath.Join(sessionDir, subagentsDir))
670		return files, baseOnly(err)
671	}
672	
673	// subAgentFiles lists agent-<id>.jsonl files directly inside dir, sorted by
674	// ID, each with its meta file if one exists. A missing dir or a symbolic
675	// link yields nothing.
676	func subAgentFiles(dir string) ([]SubAgentFiles, error) {
677		f, err := openPlain(dir, true)
678		if f == nil {
679			if err == nil || errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
680				return nil, nil
681			}
682			return nil, err
683		}
684		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
685		entries, err := f.ReadDir(-1)
686		if err != nil {
687			return nil, err
688		}
689		var out []SubAgentFiles
690		for _, e := range entries {
691			if sa, ok := subAgentEntry(dir, e); ok {
692				out = append(out, sa)
693			}
694		}
695		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].ID < out[j].ID })
696		return out, nil
697	}
698	
699	// subAgentEntry turns a directory entry into a sub-agent, if it is a
700	// regular agent-<id>.jsonl file.
701	func subAgentEntry(dir string, e os.DirEntry) (SubAgentFiles, bool) {
702		name := e.Name()
703		if !e.Type().IsRegular() || !strings.HasPrefix(name, agentPrefix) || !strings.HasSuffix(name, transcriptExt) {
704			return SubAgentFiles{}, false
705		}
706		id := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(name, agentPrefix), transcriptExt)
707		if id == "" {
708			return SubAgentFiles{}, false
709		}
710		sa := SubAgentFiles{ID: sanitizeLabel(id), Transcript: filepath.Join(dir, name)}
711		metaPath := filepath.Join(dir, agentPrefix+id+metaExt)
712		if mf, _ := openPlain(metaPath, false); mf != nil {
713			_ = mf.Close()
714			sa.Meta = metaPath
715		}
716		return sa, true
717	}
718	
719	// baseOnly rewrites a path error so it names the base name of the file, not
720	// the full path; errors.Is and errors.As on the cause keep working.
721	func baseOnly(err error) error {
722		var pe *fs.PathError
723		if errors.As(err, &pe) {
724			return &fs.PathError{Op: pe.Op, Path: filepath.Base(pe.Path), Err: pe.Err}
725		}
726		return err
727	}
728	package agentusage
729	
730	import (
731		"encoding/json"
732		"errors"
733		"io"
734	)
735	
736	// State tells whether a sub-agent has finished.
737	type State int
738	
739	const (
740		StateUnknown State = iota
741		StateFinished
742		StateUnfinished
743	)
744	
745	// meta is the subset of agent-<id>.meta.json that is read. The description
746	// and worktree path keys are deliberately absent: they are never decoded.
747	type meta struct {
748		AgentType  string
749		Finished   *bool
750		SpawnDepth int
751	}
752	
753	// wireMeta keeps every field raw: one of an unexpected type costs that field
754	// only. A finished value that is not a boolean yields StateUnknown, not an
755	// error.
756	type wireMeta struct {
757		AgentType  json.RawMessage `json:"agentType"`
758		Finished   json.RawMessage `json:"finished"`
759		SpawnDepth json.RawMessage `json:"spawnDepth"`
760	}
761	
762	// maxMetaBytes is the largest meta file read; a bigger one is refused.
763	const maxMetaBytes = 1 << 20
764	
765	// Fixed messages because encoding/json errors can quote file content.
766	var (
767		errMalformedMeta = errors.New("agentusage: malformed meta file")
768		errMetaTooBig    = errors.New("agentusage: meta file too large")
769		errMetaNotPlain  = errors.New("agentusage: meta file is not a regular file")
770	)
771	
772	// readMeta reads a meta file. A missing file yields an error satisfying
773	// errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist). A symbolic link or non-regular file is
774	// refused, and reading is bounded by maxMetaBytes.
775	func readMeta(path string) (meta, error) {
776		f, err := openPlain(path, false)
777		if err != nil {
778			return meta{}, err
779		}
780		if f == nil {
781			return meta{}, errMetaNotPlain
782		}
783		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
784		b, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, maxMetaBytes+1))
785		if err != nil {
786			return meta{}, err
787		}
788		if len(b) > maxMetaBytes {
789			return meta{}, errMetaTooBig
790		}
791		var w wireMeta
792		if json.Unmarshal(b, &w) != nil {
793			return meta{}, errMalformedMeta
794		}
795		m := meta{AgentType: sanitizeLabel(optString(w.AgentType))}
796		var fin bool
797		if json.Unmarshal(w.Finished, &fin) == nil && string(w.Finished) != "null" {
798			m.Finished = &fin // absent, null or a wrong type: stays nil
799		}
800		if len(w.SpawnDepth) > 0 {
801			_ = json.Unmarshal(w.SpawnDepth, &m.SpawnDepth) // wrong type: stays 0
802			m.SpawnDepth = max(m.SpawnDepth, 0)
803		}
804		return m, nil
805	}
806	
807	// state maps the finished flag; absent or null is StateUnknown.
808	func (m meta) state() State {
809		switch {
810		case m.Finished == nil:
811			return StateUnknown
812		case *m.Finished:
813			return StateFinished
814		}
815		return StateUnfinished
816	}
817	package agentusage
818	
819	import (
820		"strings"
821		"unicode"
822		"unicode/utf8"
823	)
824	
825	// Bounds that keep memory and output size independent of what a transcript
826	// contains.
827	const (
828		// maxFileIssuesPerFile caps the unreadable/oversized FileIssue entries
829		// kept per file; the counters keep counting past it.
830		maxFileIssuesPerFile = 100
831		// maxNoIDEntries caps the per-message table for lines without a message
832		// id. Past it a line still counts in NoMessageID, Messages and tokens,
833		// but gets no table entry.
834		maxNoIDEntries    = 100000
835		maxModelsPerAgent = 64
836		maxVersions       = 64
837		// maxLabelLen is the longest label (model, version, id, file name) kept, in bytes.
838		maxLabelLen = 128
839	)
840	
841	// sanitizeLabel cleans a short label read from disk; see sanitize.
842	func sanitizeLabel(s string) string { return sanitize(s, maxLabelLen) }
843	
844	// sanitize replaces with '?' every invalid UTF-8 byte, every control character
845	// (C0, DEL and C1, so a raw or encoded 0x9B CSI included) and every format
846	// character (category Cf: bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width marks), then
847	// truncates the result to maxLen bytes, without splitting a UTF-8 sequence
848	// when it can be avoided. Text read from disk reaches a terminal, where an
849	// escape sequence would be interpreted and a bidi override would reorder it.
850	func sanitize(s string, maxLen int) string {
851		if len(s) > maxLen {
852			cut := maxLen
853			for cut > 0 && !utf8.RuneStart(s[cut]) {
854				cut--
855			}
856			s = s[:cut]
857		}
858		var b strings.Builder
859		for _, r := range s { // an invalid byte ranges as utf8.RuneError
860			if r == utf8.RuneError || unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r) {
861				r = '?'
862			}
863			b.WriteRune(r)
864		}
865		return b.String()
866	}
867	
868	// modelSet is an insertion-ordered set of at most maxModelsPerAgent models.
869	type modelSet struct {
870		list []string
871		seen map[string]bool
872	}
873	
874	// add keeps model unless it is empty, already listed, or the set is full.
875	func (s *modelSet) add(model string) {
876		if model == "" || len(s.list) >= maxModelsPerAgent || s.seen[model] {
877			return
878		}
879		if s.seen == nil {
880			s.seen = map[string]bool{}
881		}
882		s.seen[model] = true
883		s.list = append(s.list, model)
884	}

# Agent usage — `internal/agentusage`

> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
> read this file when working on the code it describes.

Two pieces: the data layer `internal/agentusage` (sections up to
"Verification") and the `:agent-usage` view `internal/ui/agentusageview`
(last section, DEVDESK-41).

## What the package is for

`internal/agentusage` reads the transcripts Claude Code writes under its
projects directory and returns, for one session, the **token counts per
agent** (the orchestrator and each sub-agent). It is the data layer of the
agent usage monitor (DEVDESK-40, spike S-01 then step S-02).

What it does **not** do:

- no cost, price or quota computation;
- no storage, no cache, nothing written to disk;
- no UI, no Bubble Tea import (the view lives in `internal/ui/agentusageview`);
- no dependency beyond the Go standard library.

**The public API is a contract.** Every exported symbol in the table below
(`Tokens`, `Agent`, `State`, `Usage`, `Diagnostics`, `FileIssue`, `IssueKind`,
`SessionFiles`, `SubAgentFiles`, `ParseSession`, `LocateSession`, `ProjectsRoot`,
`ListSessions`, `Session`, `Listing`)
is consumed by S-03b, S-04 and S-05a. Changing a field is a change to those
stories; add, do not rename.

## Public API

| Symbol | Role |
|---|---|
| `ProjectsRoot()` | `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, else `~/.claude/projects` |
| `LocateSession(parentTranscript)` | from `<dir>/<uuid>.jsonl`, finds `<dir>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and their meta files. Returns `SessionFiles{ID, Parent, SubAgents}`. A missing session directory means no sub-agents. Returns an error if the parent is missing, is a symbolic link or is not a regular file. |
| `SessionFiles` | `ID`, `Parent` (path of the parent transcript), `SubAgents []SubAgentFiles` |
| `SubAgentFiles` | `ID`, `Transcript`, `Meta` (`""` if the meta file is absent) |
| `ParseSession(SessionFiles)` | returns `Usage`. Fails only if the parent transcript cannot be opened: a missing file, a symbolic link or a non-regular file is an **error**, not an ignored input. |
| `ListSessions(root)` | lists `<root>/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl`, one level deep, never recursively. Returns `Listing`. A missing root is an empty `Listing` and no error; a root that is not a directory or cannot be read is an error naming the base name only. The root itself may be a symbolic link (the user's own choice); anything below it may not. |
| `Session{ID, Parent, Project, ModTime}` | `Parent` is a full path, for `LocateSession`, and is never logged. `Project` is the working directory read from the transcript (`cwd`), sanitized and capped at 4096 bytes, or `""` if none. `ModTime` is the transcript's modification time. |
| `Listing{Sessions, Omitted}` | `Sessions` newest `ModTime` first, ties by ID ascending. `Omitted` counts what was not listed: linked or non-regular transcripts, linked or unreadable project directories, and sessions past the cap. |
| `Tokens{Input, Output, CacheRead, CacheWrite}` | `int64` counters; `Total()` and `Add()` saturate at `math.MaxInt64` |
| `Agent` | `ID` (empty for the orchestrator), `Main`, `Type`, `Models`, `Tokens`, `Messages`, `PartialMessages`, `State`, `SpawnDepth`; `PartialOutput()` |
| `State` | `StateUnknown`, `StateFinished`, `StateUnfinished` |
| `Usage` | `SessionID`, `Agents` (orchestrator first, then sub-agents by ID), `Versions`, `Diagnostics`; `Total()` |
| `Diagnostics` | `UnreadableLines`, `OversizedLines`, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, `MetaMissing`, `MetaUnreadable`, `TruncatedFiles`, `Files []FileIssue`; `Degraded()` |
| `FileIssue{File, Offset, Kind}` | one skipped line or file problem. `File` is a base name. `Offset` is the byte offset of the line (for `IssueReadError`, the offset consumed; for `IssueOpenFailed`, 0). Entries are sorted by offset within each file. |
| `IssueKind` | `IssueUnreadable` (not JSON, truncated, or bad counters), `IssueOversized` (longer than `MaxLineBytes`), `IssueOpenFailed` (a sub-agent transcript could not be opened), `IssueReadError` (reading stopped on an I/O error) |

`State` is read from the `finished` key of the sub-agent's meta file: `true`
is `StateFinished`, `false` is `StateUnfinished`. An absent, null or
wrongly typed key, a missing or unreadable meta file, and the orchestrator
are `StateUnknown`.

## Transcript format

```
projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl                          orchestrator
projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl     one per sub-agent
projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json agentType, finished, spawnDepth
projects/<project>/<uuid>/tool-results/                  never read
```

Each transcript line is a JSON object. Only `version` and `message.{id, model,
stop_reason, usage}` are read; the four counters are `input_tokens`,
`output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
Content, tools and descriptions are not declared in the decoding structs, so
`encoding/json` skips them without keeping them. Nothing is searched
recursively. Symbolic links are handled by position:

- a **parent transcript** that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is an
  **error** (`LocateSession` and `ParseSession`);
- a sub-agent transcript that is a link or not a regular file is not listed by
  `LocateSession`; if one is passed to `ParseSession` anyway, it stays in
  `Agents` with an `IssueOpenFailed` entry;
- a meta file that is a link or not a regular file counts as missing
  (`MetaMissing`);
- a session directory or `subagents/` directory that is a link means no
  sub-agents.

## Aggregation rules

- **Last line wins per `message.id`**, over the whole session. Streaming writes
  the same message several times; only the final state counts.
- **A message seen in several files is attributed to the last file read**
  (orchestrator first, then sub-agents sorted by ID). Each such overwrite counts
  in `Diagnostics.CrossFileDuplicates`.
- **A line without `message.id` counts once**, keyed by file and offset, and
  increments `NoMessageID`.
- **`<synthetic>` is excluded**: locally generated turns are never billed.
- **A line with neither id, model nor usage is ignored** (user and tool-result
  lines).
- **Partial output**: a message whose last line has a null or absent
  `stop_reason` is counted in `Agent.PartialMessages`, and `PartialOutput()` is
  true. Its output count is a floor. This is computed for every agent; the UI
  decides how to show it.
- **Saturation**: sums stop at `math.MaxInt64` instead of wrapping.
- An incomplete last line (no newline) is not counted and its file is listed in
  `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles`. If it already exceeds the line cap it is dropped
  silently.

## Tolerance

The format is not a documented API, so the parser degrades rather than fails.

- Unknown fields are ignored.
- A message with an id or model but **no `usage`** (absent, or renamed by a
  newer client) is counted in `Diagnostics.NoUsage` and adds nothing. A
  sub-agent with no usable meta `finished` is `StateUnknown`.
- Metadata of an unexpected type (`model`, `version`, `agentType`,
  `spawnDepth`) costs that field only, not the line.
- A counter that is negative, fractional or not a number makes the line
  unreadable (`UnreadableLines`). An absent or null counter is 0.
- A sub-agent that cannot be opened stays in `Agents` with no tokens and an
  `IssueOpenFailed` entry. A read error mid-file keeps what was read and adds
  `IssueReadError` at the offset consumed.
- A missing meta file counts in `MetaMissing`; an unreadable one in
  `MetaUnreadable`.

## Privacy

`ParseSession` returns **numeric aggregates only**. No prompt, answer, tool
input, description or path is ever stored in a `Usage`.

**Amendment (DEVDESK-41): `cwd` is now read and displayed.** `ListSessions`
alone reads it, to tell sessions apart by project. It is the first non-empty
string `cwd` found in the first 8 MiB of a transcript (twice `MaxLineBytes`, so
one maximal line can be skipped); the scan stops there and nothing else of the
transcript is kept. The view shows the **full path**, with the home folder
folded to `~`. The path is sanitized and capped, and is **never logged**: the
view logs a failed listing, but its error carries a base name only. A `Usage`
still carries no path. This replaces the earlier wording that no path was ever
read.

- Errors carry the base name of a file, never its full path (`baseOnly`), and
  fixed messages instead of `encoding/json` errors, which can quote content.
- Text that comes from disk goes through `sanitize`: labels (model, version,
  agent type, session and agent IDs, file names; `sanitizeLabel`, cut to 128
  bytes) and the `cwd` (cut to 4096 bytes). Replaced by `?`: invalid UTF-8
  bytes, every control character (C0, DEL and **C1**, so a raw or encoded
  0x9B CSI is caught) and every format character (Unicode category **Cf**:
  bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width marks). Text read from disk reaches a
  terminal, where an escape sequence would be interpreted and a bidi override
  would reorder what follows.
- `FileIssue.File` is a base name, never a path.
- The fixtures plant `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` in the `content`, `description`,
  `cwd` and tool `input` fields of the transcripts and in the `description`
  of the `.meta.json` files. Tests check that it never appears in a `Usage` or
  an error.

## Limits and caps

Memory and output size do not depend on what a transcript contains.

| Bound | Value | Behavior past it |
|---|---|---|
| Line length (`MaxLineBytes`) | 4 MiB | line skipped, counted in `OversizedLines`, never held in memory |
| `FileIssue` entries per file | 100, for `IssueUnreadable` and `IssueOversized` only | counters keep counting, entries stop. `IssueOpenFailed` and `IssueReadError` occur once per file and are always kept |
| Lines without id in the table | 100000, for the whole session (all files together) | still counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`, but aggregated without a table entry |
| Models per agent / versions per session | 64 | extra ones dropped |
| Label length | 128 bytes | truncated |
| Meta file | 1 MiB | refused (`MetaUnreadable`) |
| Sessions listed (`ListSessions`) | 10000 | the oldest are dropped and counted in `Listing.Omitted` |
| `cwd` probe (`ListSessions`) | first 8 MiB of each kept transcript | `Project` is `""` |
| `Session.Project` length | 4096 bytes | truncated |

The 10000 cap applies after the directories are read: there is **no bound on
memory or time before it**. Every entry of every project directory is read and
stat-ed first, so a very large projects tree costs that much before the cap
trims the result. Only the `cwd` probe, run on the kept sessions, is bounded.

## Known risk: a FIFO swapped in between `Lstat` and `Open`

`openPlain` (`safeopen.go`) calls `Lstat`, refuses links and non-regular
files, opens the file, then compares the handle with the `Lstat` result using
`os.SameFile`. That closes the check-then-open window for links. It does not
for a regular file replaced by a **FIFO** between `Lstat` and `Open`: `os.Open`
blocks until a writer appears, before `SameFile` can run. Closing it would need
`O_NONBLOCK`, which the `os` package does not offer portably. The window is tiny
and the attacker must already control the transcripts directory. Accepted and
documented in the code. `ListSessions` has the same exposure: it opens each
kept transcript through `openPlain` to read its `cwd`, so a FIFO swapped in
there can block the listing (and so the view's read, which runs in a `Cmd`).
Carried over unchanged, not closed.

## Diagnostics and `Degraded`

`Diagnostics.Degraded()` is true if anything was skipped or guessed: unreadable
or oversized lines, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, meta
missing or unreadable, truncated files, or any `FileIssue`. A consumer should
show the totals as usual and flag them as approximate when it is true. A new
counter must be added to `Degraded()`.

## Verification

- **Spike S-01**: the parsing rules were checked against ccusage on 3 real
  sessions, with a **0.00 %** difference.
- **Fixtures** in `internal/agentusage/testdata/` are synthetic: shape follows
  Claude Code 2.1.302, every value is invented. `v2.1.302-basic/`,
  `synthetic-other-version/` (renamed or absent usage, unknown line type) and
  `damaged/` (bad line, file cut mid-JSON). Expected totals are written by hand
  in `parse_test.go`. See `testdata/README.md`.
- **Cross-check against ccusage** (step 6 of S-02, DEVDESK-54), reference
  version `ccusage@20.0.43`. `crosscheck_test.go` compares `ParseSession` with
  a reference file and is **skipped unless `DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF` is set**
  (path of the reference file). CI never sets it, so **CI does not run this
  test**: run it by hand. `DEVDESK_CLAUDE_PROJECTS` points to the projects
  directory to read (default: `ProjectsRoot()`). Each session is looked up as
  `<root>/<project>/<id>.jsonl`.
  The reference file is produced by the `mise` task:

  ```bash
  mise run agentusage-ref -- <uuid>... > /path/outside/repo/ref.json
  DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF=/path/outside/repo/ref.json go test ./internal/agentusage -run TestSessionTotalsMatchCcusage -v
  ```

  The task needs a POSIX shell, `npx` and `jq` (no Windows), and runs with
  `set -euo pipefail`: a failing ccusage call fails the task. For each session
  id it runs `ccusage claude session --id <uuid> --json` and writes
  `{"sessions": [{id, total, input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, ...]}`,
  where `total` is ccusage's `totalTokens` and the four others are sums over its
  `entries`. Write the file **outside the repository**: it comes from real
  sessions and must never be committed.

  Only `total` is required. `input`, `output`, `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite` are
  optional per session: when present, each is compared too, and each must be
  within the tolerance (2 %, strictly below). A session whose transcript is not
  found, or whose parsing fails, fails the test.

## The `:agent-usage` view

`internal/ui/agentusageview`, opened with `:agent-usage` or `:au`. It lists the
Claude Code sessions found on this machine, newest first, and reads only where
and when a session ran (see the privacy amendment above). No token count is
shown yet.

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Project | the `cwd`, **full path** with home folded to `~` (`theme.FoldHome`, done once per row in `Update`, never in a `Cell`). Cut from the left when too narrow, so the leaf stays visible. `-` (dim) when the transcript named none. |
| Last active | the transcript's `ModTime`, local time, `2006-01-02 15:04` |
| Session | the first 8 characters of the ID. `Optional`: the first column dropped on a narrow terminal. The filter (`/`) matches the full ID. |

- **Rule 139.** The body is always `m.table.View()`. Loading, an empty
  machine and a filter with no match all leave a table with its header.
- **Header** (`GetHeaderInfo`): `Sessions` (rows visible after the filter) and,
  only when non-zero, `Skipped` (`Listing.Omitted`).
- **Footer** (Rule 128), derived on every frame with no timer, in this order:
  a failed read (red, "Failed to list Claude Code sessions — check logs"; the
  error is logged, never shown, since it can name a path), then loading (spinner,
  "Reading Claude Code sessions..."), then "No Claude Code sessions found in
  <root>" when the listing is empty before any filter.
- **Shortcuts**: `ctrl+r` Refresh, `/` Filter, `?` Help. The same keys in every
  state, none greyed (Rule 130): each always acts. `.` cycles the sort column
  and is listed in `?` only (Rule 138).
- **Reload on every entry.** The view is built once and stays cached in the
  router (`createView` stops if it already exists). The reload comes from
  `switchView` (`internal/app/command_line.go`), which calls `Init()` on every
  entry, and `Init` starts a read. The rows from the previous visit stay on
  screen until the answer arrives. Unlike `ctrl+r`, this entry reload shows no
  spinner and no "Reading..." line, because `Init` cannot set `loading` to
  true. `ctrl+r` reads again under a new generation number, and a stale answer
  (older generation) is dropped. A failed refresh keeps the previous rows: they
  are dated, not wrong.
- **Rule 110.** `listSessionsCmd` resolves `ProjectsRoot()` and calls
  `ListSessions` inside the `Cmd` and returns a message; `Update` alone touches
  the model.

Known limits: the FIFO risk and the lack of a memory or time bound before the
10000-session cap (see "Limits and caps") both apply to this view's read. Claude
Code deletes old transcripts itself (30 days by default), so older sessions
disappear from the list.
package agentusage

// Agent is the usage of one agent of a session: the orchestrator (Main) or a
// sub-agent.
type Agent struct {
	ID              string
	Main            bool
	Type            string // sub-agent type from its meta file; "" if unknown
	Models          []string
	Tokens          Tokens
	Messages        int // distinct message ids
	PartialMessages int // messages whose last line has no stop reason
	State           State
	SpawnDepth      int
}

// PartialOutput reports whether some message of the agent was still being
// written (no stop reason on its last line), so its output count is a floor.
func (a Agent) PartialOutput() bool { return a.PartialMessages > 0 }

// IssueKind classifies a line that could not be counted.
type IssueKind int

const (
	IssueUnreadable IssueKind = iota // not JSON, truncated, or bad counters
	IssueOversized                   // longer than MaxLineBytes
	IssueOpenFailed                  // a sub-agent transcript could not be opened
	IssueReadError                   // reading stopped on an I/O error at Offset
)

// FileIssue locates one skipped line. File is a base name, never a path.
type FileIssue struct {
	File   string
	Offset int64
	Kind   IssueKind
}

// Diagnostics counts what parsing skipped or had to guess.
type Diagnostics struct {
	UnreadableLines     int
	OversizedLines      int
	NoUsage             int
	NoMessageID         int
	CrossFileDuplicates int
	MetaMissing         int
	MetaUnreadable      int
	TruncatedFiles      []string
	Files               []FileIssue
}

// Degraded reports whether anything was skipped or guessed.
func (d Diagnostics) Degraded() bool {
	return d.UnreadableLines > 0 || d.OversizedLines > 0 || d.NoUsage > 0 ||
		d.NoMessageID > 0 || d.CrossFileDuplicates > 0 || d.MetaMissing > 0 ||
		d.MetaUnreadable > 0 || len(d.TruncatedFiles) > 0 || len(d.Files) > 0
}

// Usage is the parsed usage of one session.
type Usage struct {
	SessionID   string
	Agents      []Agent
	Versions    []string
	Diagnostics Diagnostics
}

// Total returns the tokens of every agent.
func (u Usage) Total() Tokens {
	var t Tokens
	for _, a := range u.Agents {
		t = t.Add(a.Tokens)
	}
	return t
}
package agentusage

// msgKey identifies one message of a session. A message with an id is keyed
// by the id alone; one without is keyed by where it was read.
type msgKey struct {
	id   string
	file string
	off  int64
}

// entry is the last state seen of one message.
type entry struct {
	agent    int
	file     string
	model    string
	tokens   Tokens
	stopNull bool
}

// aggregator folds records into per-agent totals, last line wins per
// message id. Agents must be added in a fixed order (parent, then
// sub-agents by ID); a message seen in several files goes to the last.
type aggregator struct {
	agents  []Agent
	diag    Diagnostics
	entries map[msgKey]*entry
	order   []msgKey // first appearance, for stable model order
	seen    map[string]bool
	version []string // distinct versions, first appearance order
	// fileIssues counts the capped FileIssue kinds kept per file name.
	fileIssues map[string]int
	noID       int            // table entries holding a line without message id
	spill      map[int]*spill // per agent: no-id lines past maxNoIDEntries
}

// spill totals the lines that no longer get a table entry.
type spill struct {
	tokens   Tokens
	messages int
	partial  int
	models   modelSet
}

// newAggregator starts from agents carrying their identity (ID, Main, Type,
// State, SpawnDepth); the counters are filled by add and finish.
func newAggregator(agents []Agent) *aggregator {
	return &aggregator{
		agents: agents, entries: map[msgKey]*entry{}, seen: map[string]bool{},
		fileIssues: map[string]int{}, spill: map[int]*spill{},
	}
}

// addIssue records a skipped line. Unreadable and oversized lines are kept
// at most maxFileIssuesPerFile per file (the counters are not capped); the
// other kinds occur once per file and are always kept.
func (a *aggregator) addIssue(i FileIssue) {
	if i.Kind == IssueUnreadable || i.Kind == IssueOversized {
		if a.fileIssues[i.File] >= maxFileIssuesPerFile {
			return
		}
		a.fileIssues[i.File]++
	}
	a.diag.Files = append(a.diag.Files, i)
}

// addLine decodes one line of agent agentIdx's file (file is a base name) and folds it in,
// counting what is skipped. Synthetic and ignored lines never count.
func (a *aggregator) addLine(agentIdx int, file string, off int64, line []byte) {
	r, kind := decodeLine(line)
	if kind != kindUnreadable {
		a.noteVersion(r.Version)
	}
	switch kind {
	case kindUsage:
		a.add(agentIdx, file, off, r)
	case kindNoUsage:
		a.diag.NoUsage++
	case kindUnreadable:
		a.diag.UnreadableLines++
		a.addIssue(FileIssue{File: file, Offset: off, Kind: IssueUnreadable})
	case kindIgnored, kindSynthetic:
	}
}

// noteVersion records a client version the first time it is seen, up to
// maxVersions.
func (a *aggregator) noteVersion(v string) {
	v = sanitizeLabel(v)
	if v == "" || a.seen[v] || len(a.version) >= maxVersions {
		return
	}
	a.seen[v] = true
	a.version = append(a.version, v)
}

// versions returns the distinct versions seen, in order of first appearance.
func (a *aggregator) versions() []string { return a.version }

// add folds one usage record in. file and off identify the line when the
// record has no message id.
func (a *aggregator) add(agentIdx int, file string, off int64, r record) {
	key := msgKey{id: r.MessageID}
	if r.MessageID == "" {
		key = msgKey{file: file, off: off}
		a.diag.NoMessageID++
		if a.noID >= maxNoIDEntries {
			a.addSpill(agentIdx, r)
			return
		}
		a.noID++
	}
	e, ok := a.entries[key]
	if !ok {
		e = &entry{}
		a.entries[key] = e
		a.order = append(a.order, key)
	} else if e.file != file {
		a.diag.CrossFileDuplicates++
	}
	*e = entry{agent: agentIdx, file: file, model: r.Model, tokens: r.Usage, stopNull: r.StopNull}
}

// addSpill counts a no-id line that gets no table entry.
func (a *aggregator) addSpill(agentIdx int, r record) {
	sp := a.spill[agentIdx]
	if sp == nil {
		sp = &spill{}
		a.spill[agentIdx] = sp
	}
	sp.tokens = sp.tokens.Add(r.Usage)
	sp.messages++
	if r.StopNull {
		sp.partial++
	}
	sp.models.add(r.Model)
}

// finish returns the agents with Tokens, Models, Messages and
// PartialMessages computed.
func (a *aggregator) finish() []Agent {
	models := make([]modelSet, len(a.agents))
	for i := range a.agents {
		a.agents[i].Tokens, a.agents[i].Models = Tokens{}, nil
		a.agents[i].Messages, a.agents[i].PartialMessages = 0, 0
	}
	for _, key := range a.order {
		e := a.entries[key]
		ag := &a.agents[e.agent]
		ag.Tokens = ag.Tokens.Add(e.tokens)
		ag.Messages++
		if e.stopNull {
			ag.PartialMessages++
		}
		models[e.agent].add(e.model)
	}
	for i, sp := range a.spill {
		ag := &a.agents[i]
		ag.Tokens = ag.Tokens.Add(sp.tokens)
		ag.Messages += sp.messages
		ag.PartialMessages += sp.partial
		for _, m := range sp.models.list {
			models[i].add(m)
		}
	}
	for i := range a.agents {
		a.agents[i].Models = models[i].list
	}
	return a.agents
}
package agentusage

import (
	"io"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
)

// ParseSession aggregates the usage of every agent of a session. It fails
// only if the parent transcript cannot be opened; a sub-agent that cannot be
// read stays in Agents with no tokens and a FileIssue.
func ParseSession(files SessionFiles) (Usage, error) {
	subs := append([]SubAgentFiles(nil), files.SubAgents...)
	sort.Slice(subs, func(i, j int) bool { return subs[i].ID < subs[j].ID })
	agg := newAggregator([]Agent{{Main: true, State: StateUnknown}})
	if err := parseFile(agg, 0, files.Parent); err != nil {
		return Usage{}, baseOnly(err)
	}
	for _, sa := range subs {
		agg.agents = append(agg.agents, agentFromMeta(&agg.diag, sa))
		if err := parseFile(agg, len(agg.agents)-1, sa.Transcript); err != nil {
			agg.addIssue(FileIssue{File: sanitizeLabel(filepath.Base(sa.Transcript)), Kind: IssueOpenFailed})
		}
	}
	return Usage{
		SessionID:   sanitizeLabel(files.ID),
		Agents:      agg.finish(),
		Versions:    agg.versions(),
		Diagnostics: agg.diag,
	}, nil
}

// agentFromMeta builds a sub-agent's identity from its meta file, counting
// a missing or unreadable one in diag.
func agentFromMeta(diag *Diagnostics, sa SubAgentFiles) Agent {
	ag := Agent{ID: sanitizeLabel(sa.ID)}
	if sa.Meta == "" {
		diag.MetaMissing++
		return ag
	}
	m, err := readMeta(sa.Meta)
	if err != nil {
		diag.MetaUnreadable++
		return ag
	}
	ag.Type, ag.State, ag.SpawnDepth = m.AgentType, m.state(), m.SpawnDepth
	return ag
}

// parseFile folds one transcript into the aggregator for agent idx. It
// fails only if the file cannot be opened.
func parseFile(agg *aggregator, idx int, path string) error {
	f, err := openPlain(path, false)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if f == nil {
		return errNotRegular
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
	parseReader(agg, idx, sanitizeLabel(filepath.Base(path)), f)
	return nil
}

// parseReader folds r into agg for agent idx; name is the file's sanitized
// base name. A read error mid-stream keeps what was read and is recorded as
// an IssueReadError at the offset consumed; it is not an unreadable line.
func parseReader(agg *aggregator, idx int, name string, r io.Reader) {
	start := len(agg.diag.Files)
	res, err := scanLines(r, MaxLineBytes, func(line []byte, off int64) {
		agg.addLine(idx, name, off, line)
	})
	for _, off := range res.OversizedAt {
		agg.diag.OversizedLines++
		agg.addIssue(FileIssue{File: name, Offset: off, Kind: IssueOversized})
	}
	if err != nil {
		agg.addIssue(FileIssue{File: name, Offset: res.Consumed, Kind: IssueReadError})
	}
	if len(res.Tail) > 0 {
		agg.diag.TruncatedFiles = append(agg.diag.TruncatedFiles, name)
	}
	issues := agg.diag.Files[start:]
	sort.SliceStable(issues, func(i, j int) bool { return issues[i].Offset < issues[j].Offset })
}
package agentusage

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

const (
	transcriptExt = ".jsonl"
	metaExt       = ".meta.json"
	agentPrefix   = "agent-"
	subagentsDir  = "subagents"
)

// SubAgentFiles locates one sub-agent's files; Meta is "" if absent.
type SubAgentFiles struct{ ID, Transcript, Meta string }

// SessionFiles locates a session's transcripts.
type SessionFiles struct {
	ID, Parent string
	SubAgents  []SubAgentFiles
}

// ProjectsRoot returns the Claude Code projects directory:
// $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects, else ~/.claude/projects.
func ProjectsRoot() (string, error) {
	if dir := os.Getenv("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"); dir != "" {
		return filepath.Join(dir, "projects"), nil
	}
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "projects"), nil
}

// LocateSession finds the sub-agent files of the session whose parent
// transcript is <dir>/<uuid>.jsonl, looking in <dir>/<uuid>/subagents/. A
// missing session directory means no sub-agents. Symbolic links are ignored
// and nothing is searched recursively.
func LocateSession(parentTranscript string) (SessionFiles, error) {
	base := filepath.Base(parentTranscript)
	if !strings.HasSuffix(base, transcriptExt) {
		return SessionFiles{}, fmt.Errorf("agentusage: %s does not end in %s", base, transcriptExt)
	}
	info, err := os.Lstat(parentTranscript)
	if err != nil {
		return SessionFiles{}, baseOnly(err)
	}
	if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
		return SessionFiles{}, fmt.Errorf("agentusage: %s is not a regular file", base)
	}
	id := strings.TrimSuffix(base, transcriptExt)
	if id == "" {
		return SessionFiles{}, fmt.Errorf("agentusage: %s has no session id", base)
	}
	files := SessionFiles{ID: sanitizeLabel(id), Parent: parentTranscript}
	sessionDir := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(parentTranscript), id)
	if fi, err := os.Lstat(sessionDir); err != nil || !fi.IsDir() {
		if err == nil || errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
			return files, nil // absent, or a link: no sub-agents
		}
		return files, baseOnly(err)
	}
	files.SubAgents, err = subAgentFiles(filepath.Join(sessionDir, subagentsDir))
	return files, baseOnly(err)
}

// subAgentFiles lists agent-<id>.jsonl files directly inside dir, sorted by
// ID, each with its meta file if one exists. A missing dir or a symbolic
// link yields nothing.
func subAgentFiles(dir string) ([]SubAgentFiles, error) {
	f, err := openPlain(dir, true)
	if f == nil {
		if err == nil || errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
			return nil, nil
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
	entries, err := f.ReadDir(-1)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var out []SubAgentFiles
	for _, e := range entries {
		if sa, ok := subAgentEntry(dir, e); ok {
			out = append(out, sa)
		}
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].ID < out[j].ID })
	return out, nil
}

// subAgentEntry turns a directory entry into a sub-agent, if it is a
// regular agent-<id>.jsonl file.
func subAgentEntry(dir string, e os.DirEntry) (SubAgentFiles, bool) {
	name := e.Name()
	if !e.Type().IsRegular() || !strings.HasPrefix(name, agentPrefix) || !strings.HasSuffix(name, transcriptExt) {
		return SubAgentFiles{}, false
	}
	id := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(name, agentPrefix), transcriptExt)
	if id == "" {
		return SubAgentFiles{}, false
	}
	sa := SubAgentFiles{ID: sanitizeLabel(id), Transcript: filepath.Join(dir, name)}
	metaPath := filepath.Join(dir, agentPrefix+id+metaExt)
	if mf, _ := openPlain(metaPath, false); mf != nil {
		_ = mf.Close()
		sa.Meta = metaPath
	}
	return sa, true
}

// baseOnly rewrites a path error so it names the base name of the file, not
// the full path; errors.Is and errors.As on the cause keep working.
func baseOnly(err error) error {
	var pe *fs.PathError
	if errors.As(err, &pe) {
		return &fs.PathError{Op: pe.Op, Path: filepath.Base(pe.Path), Err: pe.Err}
	}
	return err
}
package agentusage

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"io"
)

// State tells whether a sub-agent has finished.
type State int

const (
	StateUnknown State = iota
	StateFinished
	StateUnfinished
)

// meta is the subset of agent-<id>.meta.json that is read. The description
// and worktree path keys are deliberately absent: they are never decoded.
type meta struct {
	AgentType  string
	Finished   *bool
	SpawnDepth int
}

// wireMeta keeps every field raw: one of an unexpected type costs that field
// only. A finished value that is not a boolean yields StateUnknown, not an
// error.
type wireMeta struct {
	AgentType  json.RawMessage `json:"agentType"`
	Finished   json.RawMessage `json:"finished"`
	SpawnDepth json.RawMessage `json:"spawnDepth"`
}

// maxMetaBytes is the largest meta file read; a bigger one is refused.
const maxMetaBytes = 1 << 20

// Fixed messages because encoding/json errors can quote file content.
var (
	errMalformedMeta = errors.New("agentusage: malformed meta file")
	errMetaTooBig    = errors.New("agentusage: meta file too large")
	errMetaNotPlain  = errors.New("agentusage: meta file is not a regular file")
)

// readMeta reads a meta file. A missing file yields an error satisfying
// errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist). A symbolic link or non-regular file is
// refused, and reading is bounded by maxMetaBytes.
func readMeta(path string) (meta, error) {
	f, err := openPlain(path, false)
	if err != nil {
		return meta{}, err
	}
	if f == nil {
		return meta{}, errMetaNotPlain
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
	b, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, maxMetaBytes+1))
	if err != nil {
		return meta{}, err
	}
	if len(b) > maxMetaBytes {
		return meta{}, errMetaTooBig
	}
	var w wireMeta
	if json.Unmarshal(b, &w) != nil {
		return meta{}, errMalformedMeta
	}
	m := meta{AgentType: sanitizeLabel(optString(w.AgentType))}
	var fin bool
	if json.Unmarshal(w.Finished, &fin) == nil && string(w.Finished) != "null" {
		m.Finished = &fin // absent, null or a wrong type: stays nil
	}
	if len(w.SpawnDepth) > 0 {
		_ = json.Unmarshal(w.SpawnDepth, &m.SpawnDepth) // wrong type: stays 0
		m.SpawnDepth = max(m.SpawnDepth, 0)
	}
	return m, nil
}

// state maps the finished flag; absent or null is StateUnknown.
func (m meta) state() State {
	switch {
	case m.Finished == nil:
		return StateUnknown
	case *m.Finished:
		return StateFinished
	}
	return StateUnfinished
}
package agentusage

import (
	"strings"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// Bounds that keep memory and output size independent of what a transcript
// contains.
const (
	// maxFileIssuesPerFile caps the unreadable/oversized FileIssue entries
	// kept per file; the counters keep counting past it.
	maxFileIssuesPerFile = 100
	// maxNoIDEntries caps the per-message table for lines without a message
	// id. Past it a line still counts in NoMessageID, Messages and tokens,
	// but gets no table entry.
	maxNoIDEntries    = 100000
	maxModelsPerAgent = 64
	maxVersions       = 64
	// maxLabelLen is the longest label (model, version, id, file name) kept, in bytes.
	maxLabelLen = 128
)

// sanitizeLabel cleans a short label read from disk; see sanitize.
func sanitizeLabel(s string) string { return sanitize(s, maxLabelLen) }

// sanitize replaces with '?' every invalid UTF-8 byte, every control character
// (C0, DEL and C1, so a raw or encoded 0x9B CSI included) and every format
// character (category Cf: bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width marks), then
// truncates the result to maxLen bytes, without splitting a UTF-8 sequence
// when it can be avoided. Text read from disk reaches a terminal, where an
// escape sequence would be interpreted and a bidi override would reorder it.
func sanitize(s string, maxLen int) string {
	if len(s) > maxLen {
		cut := maxLen
		for cut > 0 && !utf8.RuneStart(s[cut]) {
			cut--
		}
		s = s[:cut]
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, r := range s { // an invalid byte ranges as utf8.RuneError
		if r == utf8.RuneError || unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r) {
			r = '?'
		}
		b.WriteRune(r)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// modelSet is an insertion-ordered set of at most maxModelsPerAgent models.
type modelSet struct {
	list []string
	seen map[string]bool
}

// add keeps model unless it is empty, already listed, or the set is full.
func (s *modelSet) add(model string) {
	if model == "" || len(s.list) >= maxModelsPerAgent || s.seen[model] {
		return
	}
	if s.seen == nil {
		s.seen = map[string]bool{}
	}
	s.seen[model] = true
	s.list = append(s.list, model)
}
